description: Citation-check corpus (VER-R4): bounded claim-vs-source comparison — does the cited document say what the claim says it says (numbers, period, population, direction)? An extraction-precision task, not open-web reasoning. The cited document is the OBJECT of the check, never evidence.

cases.claim: According to the Treasury's BEFU, growth will be 2.1 percent next year.

citedDocument.text: Real GDP growth is forecast to be 2.1 percent in the year ending June 2027.

cases.claim: Treasury forecasts growth of 3.4 percent next year.

citedDocument.text: Real GDP growth is forecast to be 2.1 percent in the year ending June 2027.

cases.claim: Treasury's own numbers show the economy is booming.

citedDocument.text: Real GDP growth is forecast to be 2.1 percent in the year ending June 2027.

expected.reason: the citation does not say 'booming'; the claim generalises beyond the source — the strictness binds only on what the source states

cases.claim: The Kākā's analysis says the infrastructure gap is $104b.

expected.reason: paywalled cited sources degrade to quoted-claim-only; never circumvented (ADR-0006 paywall policy)
